assumptions.choice: Used a 20-bar SMA of volume including the current bar (backtrader's standard SMA computation) as the '20-bar average volume' baseline, compared against the current bar's own volume.
assumptions.reason: Spec states 'current bar's volume is at least twice the 20-bar average volume' without specifying whether the current bar is included in the average; the standard trailing SMA reading is the most literal interpretation.

assumptions.choice: Implemented the ATR stop as an actual bt.Order.Stop order (opposite side, sized to fully close the position) submitted immediately after the entry order fills, priced at entry_fill_price -+ 2*ATR(14) evaluated at the fill bar.
assumptions.reason: Spec says stops are 'placed... at approximately 2x ATR from entry', implying a resting stop order rather than a mental/manual exit check; this is not covered by the canonical defaults so a concrete mechanism was chosen and declared.

assumptions.topic: ATR value used for stop distance
assumptions.choice: Used the ATR(14) value at the bar on which the entry order is filled (approximation of 'at entry') rather than the ATR at signal time.
assumptions.reason: The entry order fills one bar after the signal bar under the default broker; ATR at fill time is the closest available reading to 'from entry'.

assumptions.choice: On an opposite confirmed signal while a position is open, cancel any pending stop order, submit self.close() and then a new entry order (self.buy()/self.sell()) in the same next() call so both execute on the next bar's open.
assumptions.reason: Spec explicitly requires 'exit or reverse' on the opposite signal; this is the standard backtrader reversal pattern and is not covered by the canonical defaults, so it is declared explicitly.

assumptions.topic: no pyramiding on same-direction repeat signals
assumptions.choice: If already long (or short) and the same-direction confirmed signal recurs, no additional order is submitted.
assumptions.reason: Canonical default: hold at most one position at a time, no pyramiding, since the spec does not call for adding to winners.

assumptions.choice: No take-profit order was added; the only stated exit mechanisms are the ATR stop and the opposite-signal reverse/exit.
assumptions.reason: Spec only mentions ATR-based stops and opposite-signal exits/reversals; adding a take-profit would be an unstated extra rule.

assumptions.choice: The stop order price is fixed at entry (not trailed or recalculated) for the life of the position.
assumptions.reason: Spec says stops are placed 'at approximately 2x ATR from entry', with no mention of trailing, so the stop is static.

assumptions.choice: Entries use plain self.buy()/self.sell() with no size argument (default sizer); the stop order is explicitly sized to the filled entry size to ensure full closure.
assumptions.reason: Canonical default 1 for entries; the stop order's size is a mechanical necessity to fully exit the position, not a sizing policy choice.

assumptions.choice: New entry orders are blocked while self.order (the entry order) is pending, per canonical default 5; the close() order fired for a reversal is not separately tracked/guarded since it always accompanies a concurrently-submitted new entry order.
assumptions.reason: Follows the canonical order-guard convention while still allowing the close+reverse pattern the spec requires.
